history.dynasty: Multiple strata - Iron Age habitation; Satavahana, Kadamba, Chalukya, Hoysala, Vijayanagara finds (rock inscription of Kadamba founder Mayurasharma, ~345-450 CE, at the site's Bhairaweshwara/Bhairaveshvara temple)
history.period: Prehistoric (Iron Age) through Satavahana era; cave temple development later (verify)
history.summary: CSV DUPLICATE FLAG: row 483 'Ankali Mutt' is the SAME site - recommend dedup (details there). The Chandravalli cave temple (also called Ankali Mutt, since saints from Ankalagi, Belgaum district, came here to meditate) is a semilunar cave set between two giant monolithic rocks, about 3 km from Chitradurga in a valley formed by the Chitradurga, Kirabanakallu (Cholagudda) and Jolagudda hills. Chandravalli ('moon-shaped', formerly Chandanavati) is a major prehistoric archaeological site: excavations by R. Narasimhachar with B.L. Rice and R. Shamasastry (1909), M.H. Krishna (1928-30) and Mortimer Wheeler for the ASI (1947) revealed painted pottery, earthen pots and coins of the Satavahana, Vijayanagara and Hoysala dynasties, Roman denarii of Emperor Augustus and a Chinese Han coin of Emperor Wu Ti (2nd century BC), plus neoliths and a cist burial. A rock inscription of Kadamba founder Mayurasharma (~345-450 CE) stands in the Bhairaweshwara temple at the site; Chandravalli is described as the first capital of the Kadambas. The cave - reached about 80 ft below/above local grade per reports (verify) - has a Shivalinga chamber, a visitors' room, a room for sadhus, prehistoric paintings/carvings, pooja room and bedroom; lore links the Panchalingeshwara shrine here to the Pandavas (five lingas installed during exile - per a 2026 travel report; verify). It is under ASI protection; a lake and forest beside the cave add bird-watching interest.

name: Chandravalli Cave Temple
town: Chandravalli (CSV town 'Chitradurga' is the district/city; the site is ~3 km from Chitradurga city)
town_description: Chandravalli is a valley site about 3 km from Chitradurga city, formed by the Chitradurga, Kirabanakallu (Cholagudda) and Jolagudda hills. A lake beside the cave temple and the surrounding forest make it a good bird-watching spot; the prehistoric settlement area excavated measures ~730 m x 730 m.

travel.road: From Chitradurga bus stand take a local taxi or auto-rickshaw (~2.9 km); ~500 m walk from the entrance to the cave; guides ~Rs 300 (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; visit in the morning - carry a torch (interiors are pitch dark, though ventilated and cool).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported 10:30 AM-5:30 PM (verify); free entry and parking reported (verify); beware of monkeys; not ideal for the claustrophobic.
